sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: hydroplaning versus wet brakes, fog lights-off versus dust and glare lights-on, locked wheels, headlight distances and wrong-way responses
Look-alike numbers and responses from the flood, fog, winter, headlight and wrong-way pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec17-R01 | anchor: A01
During a hydroplane you do not brake at all, while after driving through water you test the brakes and dry them by gently holding the pedal as you accelerate slowly. [A01]
Why it matters: group water and brakes; difficulty three; confusable sec17-F01 versus sec17-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec17-R02 | anchor: A01
Being removed from a flooded road may bring a charge for response costs, and going around a flood barricade makes the driver liable for those costs. [A01]
Why it matters: group flood liability; difficulty two; confusable sec17-F07 versus sec17-F12.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec17-R03 | anchor: A01
In fog you drive on low beams, but if you pull off the road to wait it out you turn the headlights off. [A01]
Why it matters: group fog; difficulty two; confusable sec17-F15 versus sec17-F18.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec17-R04 | anchor: A01
On slippery surfaces the car answers steering better than braking, because rolling front tires keep the most traction. [A01]
Why it matters: group traction; difficulty two; prereq sec17-F22.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec17-R05 | anchor: A02
If the wheels lock on ice you ease slightly off the brake but do not release it fully, then brake and ease off again. [A02]
Why it matters: group ice braking; difficulty three; confusable sec17-F24 versus sec17-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec17-R06 | anchor: A02
High beams on a highway must be dimmed for an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet, while low beams are needed within 200 feet of a car you follow. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlight distances; difficulty three; confusable sec17-F38 versus sec17-F40.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec17-R07 | anchor: A02
Low beams belong on city or town streets and in glare, rain or dust, while high beams are only for highways with no close oncoming traffic. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlight choice; difficulty two; confusable sec17-F37 versus sec17-F38.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec17-R08 | anchor: A02
At dusk you switch on headlights rather than parking lights, and from sunset to sunrise headlights are required by law. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlight timing; difficulty two; confusable sec17-F34 versus sec17-F35.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec17-R09 | anchor: A02
Bridges and shady spots ice over first, and packed snow should be treated much like ice. [A02]
Why it matters: group winter surfaces; difficulty two; confusable sec17-F30 versus sec17-F29.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec17-R10 | anchor: A03
Wrong-way drivers usually travel in the left or HOV lane even though they enter the highway from the right by an off-ramp. [A03]
Why it matters: group wrong-way drivers; difficulty three; prereq sec17-F49.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec17-R11 | anchor: A03
Seeing a wrong-way vehicle coming at you means ease off the gas and steer away, while seeing an overhead wrong-way alert means head for the nearest exit. [A03]
Why it matters: group wrong-way responses; difficulty two; confusable sec17-F51 versus sec17-F55.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec17-R12 | anchor: A03
Highway hypnosis is fought with rest when tired, the radio and fresh air, and an hourly stop to walk. [A03]
Why it matters: group fatigue; difficulty one; prereq sec17-F43.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0058]
